keyQuotes: They did it too well, and so it stopped being a good business.
Consumers choosing brands because of autonomous driving ultimately never happened.
In the past, price wars were like fighting a battle for a day—when dawn broke, order was restored. Now it's been three years.

mainPoints.explanation: Consumers prioritize price, space, and exterior design when purchasing vehicles, assigning low weight to autonomous driving—some even request 'without autonomy, 10,000–20,000 yuan cheaper'—rendering massive corporate investments unable to command premiums.
mainPoints.point: Intelligent driving failed to become a core differentiator for automakers.

mainPoints.explanation: From sales staff subsidizing commissions out of pocket and dealerships cutting coffee costs, to suppliers enduring dozens of bidding rounds and annual price reductions, costs have been pushed to the limit while risks rise, plunging the industry into irrational competition.
mainPoints.point: Price wars have transmitted from complete vehicles to the entire industry chain, compressing profits and elevating risks.

mainPoints.explanation: Severe product homogenization has all models converging toward design templates; prolonged subsidies have bred overcapacity that proves difficult to liquidate, fundamentally challenging the industry's profit model—a transformation previously witnessed in television and aviation.
mainPoints.point: Once technology became 'good enough,' NEVs ceased to be a good business.

oneSentenceSummary: Based on extensive first-hand interviews, this article deeply analyzes how China's NEV industry has fallen into a trap of homogenization, price wars, and declining profits, noting that intelligent driving has failed to deliver differentiation and long-term competition has transformed the sector from a 'good business' into a 'tedious, grueling one.'
originalTitle: 新能源车的困倦时代：看不到战争结束，就先迎来乏味
summary: Using Tesla's cancellation of the Model 2 as a starting point, the article systematically examines the predicament of China's NEV industry from 2024 to the present. Intelligent driving was once the core battleground for differentiation, but after massive R&D investments, automakers found consumers unwilling to pay for it—autonomy became standard equipment without premium pricing. The price war has persisted for three years, spreading from complete vehicles to sales and the supply chain, with stringent sales targets, dealer losses, and suppliers forced below cost. Industry subsidies have exceeded 1.5 trillion yuan, incubating a complete supply chain but failing to prevent overcapacity. Once technology became 'good enough,' NEVs transformed from a world-changing dream into a thin-margin grind. Drawing on extensive practitioner interviews and industry data (BYD's profit decline, Zhongsheng's losses, autonomous driving engineers changing careers), the article captures the industry's shift from entrepreneurial passion to weary resignation, maintaining a cautious outlook on future consolidation.
title: The Age of Fatigue in NEVs: Before the War Ends, Boredom Arrives
